newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Rwandan Foreign Minister opposes peacekeeping force.
newsitem.headline: Rwandan Foreign Minister opposes peacekeeping force.

text.p: Rwandan Foreign Minister Anastase Gasana said on Friday Rwanda had no need of an international peacekeeping force on its territory to help protect refugees returning from strife-stricken Zaire.
He said he was open to the idea of such a force in neighbouring Zaire, which accuses Rwanda, Burundi and Uganda of sending troops into eastern Zaire to wage war against the Zairean army.

"It's on the side of the Zairean territory that the international community needs to create a force to protect its population. We do not need any kind of force. The problems are not on our side, but on the other side," he told Belgian radio.

"The refugees are in Zaire and it's there that the Zairean intimidators are exerting pressure, it's there that the Zairean forces are stopping them (the refugees) from taking the road to Rwanda," he said, saying his country would welcome the establishment of humanitarian corridors.
Earlier on Belgian radio he had denied that Rwandan government troops were involved in fighting in eastern Zaire, but said they were ready to defend their country against Zairean attacks.
